message.reasoning:
S: file written to disk, no browser user — but stored XSS awaiting a victim; integrity of subsequent system... the file itself is the same host. SC/VC: no confidentiality impact; SI/SVI: report file integrity affected but low. I'll set SI=L (the written report file is modified), VI=N, and note the user must open the file (UI:P). AV:L (CLI/local lab), AT:N (attacker-influenced text passes through model), PR:L? No auth on tools at all — PR:N within the single-agent lab. UI:P since a person must open the report. VA:N.

AISS: LC=D (attacker text to tool call), CP=N (report is re-retrieved output only, no memory altered), AP=N (single agent, output file), RH=N (tests are outside, no reward channel), ES=M (tool allowlist exists but no argument schemas).

Verify episodes: automated test writes malicious HTML confirmed by parser. The PoC test at tests/test_s5_output_handling.py:94-97 directly calls write_report with a script payload and parses the output file with HTMLParser to confirm active content. This is production-equivalent (in-process tool call, no mocked components) and human-verified (the packet asserts the parser finds active content). So verified_episodes=1, reviewed=1, reachable_proxy=false, isolation_verified=true (no reward or evaluator channel on this path; the only consumer is a browser user), so RH=N.

AP=N because the effect is confined to the initially affected component: the write_report tool and the file it produces. No trust boundary is crossed by agent logic itself; the XSS victim is scored separately as SA per the rubric note that downstream impact goes to CVSS S-metrics.

automatable=No: payload is deterministic and the PoC test is automated, but the impact requires a human to open report.html in a browser; per BOD 26-04 this makes it not fully automatable since human interaction is required.

technical_impact=Partial: the agent still functions; only report content is compromised.

applicability_as_implemented and as_modeled: model_directed_goal_pursuit=true and selects_or_sequences_actions=true for both, because the default Anthropic model and even the scripted worst-case model both choose tools, arguments, and order within the loop.

Confidence: high across metrics given the citations.
